### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know or dive deeper into any part that interests you. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work) and set a budget. | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Choose Components** | Pick CPU, motherboard, RAM, GPU, storage, PSU, case, cooling, OS. | • **CPU + Motherboard**: Match socket (e.g., Intel LGA 1200, AMD AM4).
• **RAM**: DDR4/DDR5, 16 GB is a good baseline.
• **GPU**: Depends on workload; 1080p gaming ~ RTX 3060.
• **Storage**: SSD for OS (NVMe preferred), HDD for bulk.
• **PSU**: 80+ Bronze or better, 500–650 W for mid‑range builds.
• **Case**: ATX mid‑tower, ensure airflow. | | 3 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | Screwdrivers (Phillips #0/#1), anti‑static wrist strap, clean surface. | Work on a non‑conductive surface (wood table). | | 4 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove side panels, install standoffs for motherboard. | Keep screws organized; label them if you’re using many. | | 5 | **Install the CPU** | Align the pin/landing pattern, gently place, lock. | Don’t force; use the lever or latch. | | 6 | **Apply Thermal Paste** | Spread a pea‑size amount on CPU. | Avoid over‑application; too much paste can spill onto motherboard. | | 7 | **Mount CPU Cooler** | Attach fan or liquid cooler, connect power cable. | Ensure fans face the right direction (intake vs exhaust). | | 8 | **Insert RAM** | Snap sticks into DIMM slots. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel mode. | | 9 | **Mount Motherboard** | Align with standoffs, screw down. | Double‑check that all ports line up with case cutouts. | |10 | **Install Storage** | Mount SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot. | Secure with screws or tool‑free brackets. | |11 | **Install Power Supply** | Place PSU, secure, route cables. | Keep cables tidy; use cable ties or Velcro straps. | |12 | **Connect Power Cables** | 24‑pin ATX, 8‑pin EPS, PCIe for GPU, SATA for drives. | Label cables if you’re unsure where they go. | |13 | **Install GPU** | Insert into PCIe x16 slot, secure, connect 6/8‑pin power. | Make sure the slot is fully seated. | |14 | **Add Additional Fans / Cooling** | Mount case fans, connect to motherboard headers. | Consider front intake, rear exhaust for airflow. | |15 | **Cable Management** | Route cables behind motherboard tray, use ties. | Good airflow reduces heat; also looks cleaner. | |16 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Verify all cables, no loose screws, no metal touching components. | Inspect for dust or debris. | |17 | **Power On & BIOS** | Connect monitor, keyboard, power button. Turn on. | Enter BIOS (usually F2, Del, Esc) to confirm component detection. | |18 | **Update BIOS & Drivers** | Download latest firmware from motherboard site. | Install chipset, GPU, audio drivers. | |19 | **Install Operating System** | Boot from USB installer (Windows, Linux). | Format SSD, install OS, then drivers. | |20 | **Test & Benchmark** | Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark) to ensure stability. | Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | |21 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep drivers updated, clean dust every few months. | Use a static‑safe cleaning brush for vents. | --- #### Quick Component Checklist (Mid‑Range Gaming Build) | Component | Example | Approx. Price | |-----------|---------|---------------| | CPU | AMD Ryzen 5 5600X | $200 | | Motherboard | MSI B550-A PRO | $120 | | RAM | Corsair Vengeance LPX 16 GB DDR4-3200 | $70 | | GPU | NVIDIA RTX 3060 | $330 | | SSD | Samsung 970 EVO Plus 1 TB NVMe | $110 | | HDD | Seagate Barracuda 2 TB | $55 | | PSU | EVGA 600 W1, 80+ WHITE | $50 | | Case | NZXT H510 | $70 | | Total | | ~$1,065 | *(Prices vary; check current deals.)* --- #### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **CPU not seated** | Re‑align, ensure lever clicks. | | **GPU not fully inserted** | Push until click, secure screws. | | **Short circuit** | Check for stray screws, ensure standoffs are correct. | | **No POST** | Verify power connectors, reset CMOS. | | **Overheating** | Improve airflow, reapply thermal paste. | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Compatibility checker, price alerts. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard and PSU manuals. --- ### Final Thought Building a PC is as rewarding as it is educational. Take your time, double‑check each step, and enjoy the process of creating something tailored to your needs. Happy building!
